answer: Require every agent to post a refundable copper-equivalent stake before it can trade, and tie that stake to a single ferrous identity anchor verified through ongoing work, not just a new keypair. New identities start with a narrow plume of permissions: they can quote but cannot settle large orders until peers attest to useful, non-duplicated work over several epochs. Because creating many identities multiplies the stake and the waiting cost while the permission plume stays small, a Sybil operator gains little throughput per fake account, and honest agents keep most settlement capacity.
